name: Bias in Gender Bias Benchmarks: How Spurious Features Distort Evaluation
description: Gender bias in vision-language foundation models (VLMs) raises concerns about their safe deployment and is typically evaluated using benchmarks with gender annotations on real-world images. However, as these benchmarks often contain spurious correlations between gender and non-gender features, such as objects and backgrounds, we identify a critical oversight in gender bias evaluation: Do spurious features distort gender bias evaluation? To address this question, we systematically perturb non-gender features across four widely used benchmarks (COCO-gender, FACET, MIAP, and PHASE) and various VLMs to quantify their impact on bias evaluation. Our findings reveal that even minimal perturbations, such as masking just 10% of objects or weakly blurring backgrounds, can dramatically alter bias scores, shifting metrics by up to 175% in generative VLMs and 43% in CLIP variants. This suggests that current bias evaluations often reflect model responses to spurious features rather than gender bias,
reputation: A recent research benchmark paper rather than a long-established community standard, but it targets widely used gender-bias evaluation sets in vision-language models.
notes: Evaluates sensitivity of bias metrics to spurious non-gender features; not a standard accuracy benchmark and results are highly perturbation-dependent.
